items.example: Hey, guys! Who wants pizza?
items.simple: A friendly hello to two or more people.
dialogue: A: Everyone is here at the flat.
B: Hey, guys! Who wants pizza?

items.example: Dude, check out my new shoes.
items.simple: A friendly word for a man or a friend.
dialogue: A: What is it, Tom?
B: Dude, check out my new shoes.
items.note: Brooklyn Nine-Nine ve Malcolm in the Middle'da çok sık.

items.example: Come here, buddy. I need help.
items.exampleTr: Gel buraya dostum. Yardıma ihtiyacım var.
items.simple: A very good friend. You can also use it to call someone nicely.
dialogue: A: Dad, what do you want?
B: Come here, buddy. I need help.
items.note: Friends'te sık; erkekler arasında samimi hitap.

items.example: I have a lot of stuff in my bag.
items.simple: Things that you do not name. Many things together.
dialogue: A: Why is your bag so heavy?
B: I have a lot of stuff in my bag.

items.example: You know what? Let's just go.
items.simple: You say this before you say something new or big.
dialogue: A: The queue is so long.
B: You know what? Let's just go.
items.note: The Office ve HIMYM'de konuşmayı başlatır.

items.example: I mean, it's okay, but not great.
items.exampleTr: Yani, fena değil ama harika da değil.
items.simple: You say this when you want to say your idea better.
dialogue: A: So, do you like the soup?
B: I mean, it's okay, but not great.

items.example: It's just, you know, a long day.
items.simple: A small filler. You say it while you think of words.
dialogue: A: Why are you so quiet today?
B: It's just, you know, a long day.

items.example: Yeah, I guess he's nice.
items.simple: You say this when you are not completely sure.
dialogue: A: Is your new boss a nice man?
B: Yeah, I guess he's nice.
items.note: Malcolm in the Middle ve Friends'te sık.

items.example: I'm kind of hungry. You?
items.simple: A little. Not completely.
dialogue: A: Do you want to eat something?
B: I'm kind of hungry. You?
items.note: "Kinda" şeklinde de duyulur; The Big Bang Theory'de sık.

items.example: I don't care. Pick any movie.
items.simple: You say this when it is not important to you.
dialogue: A: Which movie do you want to see?
B: I don't care. Pick any movie.
items.note: Malcolm in the Middle'da gençler çok söyler.

items.example: Good luck! Call me after the test.
items.exampleTr: İyi şanslar! Sınavdan sonra ara beni.
items.simple: You say this to wish someone a good result.
dialogue: A: I have a big test tomorrow.
B: Good luck! Call me after the test.

items.example: Check this out. I made a cake.
items.simple: You say this to show something to someone.
dialogue: A: Wait, Amy, come to the kitchen.
B: Check this out. I made a cake.

items.example: Give me a second. I'm almost ready.
items.simple: You say this when you need a very short time.
dialogue: A: Are you ready to go?
B: Give me a second. I'm almost ready.
items.note: Her dizide; "Give me a minute" da olur.

items.example: You okay? You look sad.
items.simple: A short way to ask if someone is fine.
dialogue: A: Hmm.
B: You okay? You look sad.
items.note: "Are you" düşer; The Office ve Friends'te günlük.

items.example: I'm home! What's for dinner?
items.simple: You say this when you come into your house.
dialogue: A: Is that you, Jake?
B: I'm home! What's for dinner?
items.note: Modern Family ve Malcolm in the Middle'da kapıdan girerken.

items.example: What's going on? Why is everyone here?
items.simple: You ask this when you see something strange.
dialogue: A: The room is full of people.
B: What's going on? Why is everyone here?

items.example: Who's there? Hello?
items.simple: You ask this when someone is at the door or in the dark.
dialogue: A: Knock, knock, knock.
B: Who's there? Hello?

items.example: Let me see. Oh, that looks bad.
items.simple: You say this when you want to look at something.
dialogue: A: I cut my finger on the box.
B: Let me see. Oh, that looks bad.

items.example: Be right back. I need water.
items.simple: You say this when you leave for a very short time.
dialogue: A: Where are you going?
B: Be right back. I need water.

items.example: Here you go. Your coffee.
items.simple: You say this when you give something to someone.
dialogue: A: Thanks! I really need a coffee.
B: Here you go. Your coffee.

items.example: Sit tight. I'll be there soon.
items.simple: You say this to tell someone to wait and stay.
dialogue: A: My car broke down on the road!
B: Sit tight. I'll be there soon.

items.example: Any news? Did he call?
items.exampleTr: Yeni bir şey var mı? Aradı mı?
items.simple: You ask this to find out if something new happened.
dialogue: A: I am waiting for Mark.
B: Any news? Did he call?

items.example: Take it easy. See you on Monday.
items.simple: You say this when you say goodbye, or to say "relax".
dialogue: A: Okay, I am going home now.
B: Take it easy. See you on Monday.

items.example: Long day. Sit down and rest.
items.simple: You say this when the day was hard or tiring.
dialogue: A: Ugh, I just got in. Wow, I am tired.
B: Long day. Sit down and rest.

items.example: Let's grab a coffee after work.
items.simple: To go and get a coffee quickly, often with a friend.
dialogue: A: Do you have time later?
B: Let's grab a coffee after work.
